components.what: additive attention bias encoding the graph, broadcast-added to the [B, N, N] scores before the softmax; passed unchanged to every head of every layer; its values are built by the caller (not in REPO)
first layer: n_heads[0] attn_head calls on `inputs`, each out_sz=hid_units[0], activation (ELU by default), residual=False; heads concatenated
intermediate layers i = 1 .. len(hid_units)-1 (none if len(hid_units) == 1): n_heads[i] attn_head calls on h_1, out_sz=hid_units[i], activation, residual=residual; heads concatenated
output (prediction) layer: n_heads[-1] attn_head calls on h_1, out_sz=nb_classes, identity activation, residual=False; heads averaged
one dense attention head; called once per head in every layer (gat.py lines 12, 20, 26); each call builds its own tf.layers.conv1d weights, so W and a are separate per head
dropout on the head input with keep prob 1 - in_drop, only if in_drop != 0.0; its output replaces `seq`, so the residual branch also sees it
kernel-size-1 conv without bias = the shared linear map W applied to every node; seq_fts = W h, [B, N, F'=out_sz]
the attention-score computation (code comment: 'simplest self-attention possible'): two width-1 projections of W h, pairwise broadcast sum, LeakyReLU
first half of a: a width-1 conv on W h giving one score per node (the attending node i), f_1 [B, N, 1]; conv1d bias left at its default
second half of a: a separate width-1 conv on W h giving one score per node (the neighbour j), f_2 [B, N, 1], transposed to [B, 1, N]
broadcast addition [B, N, 1] + [B, 1, N] -> [B, N, N]: score for every pair (i, j), equal to a^T [W h_i || W h_j] with a split into two halves; this replaces an explicit concatenation
LeakyReLU on the pair scores, giving e_ij [B, N, N]; the slope is not passed, so the library default applies
additive masking: bias_mat is added to the dense [B, N, N] e_ij after the LeakyReLU and before the softmax; the scores are computed for all N x N pairs
softmax over the last axis (neighbours j) of the masked scores, giving the attention coefficients alpha, coefs [B, N, N]
dropout on the attention coefficients with keep prob 1 - coef_drop, only if coef_drop != 0.0
dropout on the transformed features W h before aggregation, keep prob 1 - in_drop, only if in_drop != 0.0
matrix multiply [B, N, N] x [B, N, F'] -> [B, N, F']: each node's attention-weighted sum of its neighbours' W h_j
learnable bias added to the aggregated features, ret [B, N, F']
kernel-size-1 conv projecting the head input to F' for the residual, only if residual and the input width differs from F'

unclear: REPO is partial: only models/gat.py and utils/layers.py. models.base_gattn.BaseGAttN (imported at gat.py:5), the training script, the data loading, the bias_mat construction and the loss are not in REPO. So the values of n_heads, hid_units, ffd_drop, attn_drop and residual, and what bias_mat holds, are not determined by the code.

There is no explicit concatenation [W h_i || W h_j]. The code splits a into two width-1 convs (f_1 for i, f_2 for j) and adds them by broadcasting: a^T[x||y] = a_1^T x + a_2^T y. The draft's concat_ij and a_proj map to a_proj_1, a_proj_2 and pair_sum; concat_ij has no code counterpart. Neither conv sets use_bias, so each keeps its library-default bias; their sum is the same for every j and cancels in the softmax.

Masked attention (left open in the draft): the code computes scores for all N x N pairs (dense), applies LeakyReLU, then adds bias_mat before the softmax. Masking is an additive bias on e_ij, not a restriction on which pairs enter a. Whether bias_mat is 0 on neighbours and very negative elsewhere, and whether it includes self-loops, is set by the caller (not in REPO).

The draft's single gat_layer appears three times in GAT.inference: the first layer (concatenation), the intermediate-layer loop (concatenation, optional residual; absent if len(hid_units) == 1) and the output layer (averaging). Recorded as gat_layer_1, gat_layer_i and gat_layer_out. attn_head (head) is shared by all three, so its parent is null.

Code-only parts not in the paper text: a learnable bias after aggregation (bias_add, layers.py:25), an optional residual with a width-1 conv projection when widths differ (layers.py:28-32), and dropout on W h before aggregation (layers.py:22) in addition to input and coefficient dropout. The residual uses `seq` after input dropout, because layers.py:9 reassigns seq.

The output layer applies the identity per head, averages, and returns logits. The draft's final_sigma (softmax/sigmoid after averaging, Eq. 6) is not in REPO and may sit in the absent BaseGAttN or training code, so it has no component here.
h_out (h_1) is an intermediate tensor of the model, so its role is 'data', while the draft's role is 'io'. The model's real output is logits.
Shapes: rank 3 [B, N, F] follows from conv1d over axis 1 and tf.transpose(f_2, [0, 2, 1]). The sizes of B, N and F are not determined. GAT.inference's nb_nodes and training arguments are unused.

The dropout branches are Python tests (`if in_drop != 0.0`). If the caller passes the rates as tensors rather than floats (caller not in REPO), the test does not depend on the fed value. Whether the dropout ops then always exist cannot be settled from REPO.

utils/layers.py also defines sp_attn_head (lines 38-85), a sparse variant (sparse adj_mat, sparse softmax, batch size 1 only) with the same structure. GAT.inference does not call it, so it is not recorded as components.
